items.title_en: AV-FABLE: Audio-Visual Manipulation Forensics in Long-Form Videos
items.title_zh: AV-FABLE：长视频中的音视频篡改取证基准
items.abstract_en: Localized AI manipulations in long-form videos often affect brief events within otherwise authentic content, making video-level classification insufficient for forensic analysis. Existing audio-visual deepfake benchmarks largely focus on short talking-head clips, while long-form temporal forensics remains predominantly visual. We introduce AV-FABLE, a dual-timeline benchmark for sparse manipulations in open-scene long-form audio-visual videos. AV-FABLE contains 16,650 pristine--manipulated twin pairs (998 hours) created with 27 editing configurations, with separate audio and visual timelines that enable modality-specific temporal localization and expose errors hidden by joint-timeline evaluation. On AV-FABLE, zero-shot prompting of audio-visual large language models (AV-LLMs) yields near-chance detection and poor temporal localization. In contrast, supervised readouts of their frozen perception features recover strong forensic signals, suggesting manipulation evidence is encoded in these representations but not effectively exposed through language outputs. Motivated by this observation, we propose NFSR(Native Forensics via Separated Readouts), which reads frozen AV-LLM features with separate audio and visual temporal decoders. NFSR achieves the best audio-visual localization performance in-domain and across all three out-of-distribution settings, including transfer to held-out videos from an external long-video forensic benchmark. AV-FABLE, code, and model weights will be publicly released.
items.abstract_zh: 长视频中经局部 AI 篡改的内容往往只是真实素材中短暂的事件片段，因此仅做视频级分类不足以支撑取证分析。现有音视频深度伪造基准多集中于短视频说话人片段，长视频时序取证也主要局限于视觉模态。为此，作者提出 AV-FABLE——一个面向开放场景长视频中稀疏篡改的双时间线基准，包含 16,650 对原始—篡改配对视频（共 998 小时），由 27 种编辑配置生成，且音频与视觉时间线相互独立，从而支持按模态分别进行时序定位，并暴露联合时间线评测所掩盖的错误。在该基准上，音视频大语言模型（AV-LLM）的零样本提示检测近乎随机、时序定位很差；而对其冻结感知特征做有监督读出则能恢复强取证信号，说明篡改证据已编码于表征中但未能通过语言输出体现。基于此作者提出 NFSR（分离读出的原生取证），用独立的音频与视觉时序解码器读取冻结的 AV-LLM 特征，在同域及三种分布外设置（含迁移至外部长视频取证基准的留出视频）下均取得最佳音视频定位性能。
items.highlight_zh: 双时间线长视频音视频取证基准，配合分离读出的冻结特征解码方法
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：当一段长视频里只有几秒钟的画面或声音被 AI 篡改时，传统“整段视频真/假”的判断远远不够，取证系统需要指出“哪一段、在音频还是视觉上”被改。但现有的音视频深度伪造数据集大多是短视频、以人脸说话为主，长视频取证也基本只看画面。

方法与数据：作者构建了 AV-FABLE 基准，包含 16,650 对“原始—篡改”孪生视频，总时长 998 小时，用 27 种编辑配置生成，覆盖开放场景而非说话人特写。关键设计是把音频时间线和视觉时间线拆开标注，这样可以分别评估模型在声音和画面上定位篡改的能力，而不是把两者混为一谈而掩盖错误。

实验结果：直接让音视频大模型（AV-LLM）做零样本问答，检测准确率接近随机猜测，时间定位也很差；但如果把这些模型冻结的感知特征拿出来，接上简单的有监督分类/回归读出，取证信号立刻变得很强。说明模型“看见了”篡改痕迹，只是说不出来。

提出的方法：NFSR（Native Forensics via Separated Readouts）用一个音频时序解码器和一个视觉时序解码器分别读取冻结的 AV-LLM 特征。它在同分布测试和三种分布外场景下都取得最佳的音视频定位表现，其中还包括迁移到另一个外部长视频取证基准的未见视频。

为何重要：它指出“大模型的语言输出不等于其内部知识”，并给出一个便宜可行的补救方案——不微调大模型，只训练轻量读出层；同时提供长视频、稀疏篡改、双模态时间线的标准评测，推动取证研究从短视频人脸走向真实长视频场景。基准、代码与权重将公开。

rm.usage: 长视频音视频篡改取证，与自瞄、导航、决策等环节毫无交集，赛场上也用不到伪造检测。关联很弱。

items.title_en: EmbodiedLab: Benchmarking Embodied Agents That Act to Know
items.title_zh: EmbodiedLab：评测“以行动求认知”的具身智能体基准
items.abstract_en: Embodied agents are expected to accomplish real-world goals by deciding for themselves how and when to interact with their surroundings. For many such goals, changing the physical state of the world is the means rather than the end: the agent changes the state of a system through interaction, observes the feedback, and explores until it either achieves the goal itself (e.g., discovering physical laws) or learns what the goal requires; it acts to know. Manipulation benchmarks stop at acting to change, with the target state given; scientific discovery benchmarks evaluate knowing but replace physical experimentation with symbolic actions or numerical queries. We introduce EmbodiedLab, a benchmark in which a robot must act to know. Quantitative science experiments make this setting controllable: the parameters of the system are resampled for every instance, so the result cannot be known in advance, yet it can be scored exactly. Across 30 experiments in five disciplines on 14 apparatus platforms, the agent receives an objective and the apparatus, chooses its own procedure, and operates a physics-based simulated laboratory, reading the instruments through its cameras. Evaluation checks what the agent came to know, grounded in readings recorded during the episode, as well as the physical state the task requires; every experiment is verified to be solvable. We evaluate six frontier models in their developers' coding agents with native observation and control, with added perception and motion planning, and with manipulation skills distilled from the strongest agents. With native control, even the strongest agent succeeds less than half the time; for every agent, most failures arise in interacting with the apparatus, and manipulation skills help weaker agents more than perception and planning. The benchmark and its evaluation code are available at https://github.com/HexaFuture/EmbodiedLab.
items.abstract_zh: 具身智能体应能自主决定何时、如何与环境交互来完成真实目标。对许多目标而言，改变世界状态只是手段而非目的：智能体通过交互改变系统状态、观察反馈、不断探索，直到达成目标（例如发现物理规律）或弄清目标所需条件，即“以行动求知”。现有操作类基准止步于“以行动改变”，且目标状态已给定；科学发现类基准则评测“知”，却用符号动作或数值查询替代真实物理实验。作者提出 EmbodiedLab：机器人在其中必须靠行动获知。定量科学实验使这一设定可控——每个实例的系统参数都会重新采样，结果无法预先得知，却能精确评分。基准涵盖 5 个学科、14 种实验装置平台上的 30 个实验，智能体获得目标与装置后自行决定流程，在基于物理的仿真实验室中操作，并通过相机读取仪器。评测既检查智能体最终“知道了什么”（以其在回合中记录到的读数作为依据），也检查任务要求的物理状态；每个实验均经验证可解。作者在开发者提供的编程智能体中评测六个前沿模型，分别采用原生观测与控制、增加感知与运动规划、以及从最强智能体蒸馏出的操作技能三种配置。原生控制下即使最强智能体成功率也不足一半；对每个智能体，多数失败发生在与装置交互环节，且操作技能对较弱智能体的帮助大于感知增强。
items.highlight_zh: 首个要求机器人通过物理实验主动“求知”并可精确评分的基准
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：现在的机器人基准大致分两类。一类是操作任务，比如“把杯子放到架子上”——目标状态已经告诉你了，机器人只需动手；另一类是科学发现任务，评测的是“知不知道某个规律”，但往往用符号动作或数值查询代替真实实验。中间那种更真实的能力被忽略了：机器人需要通过动手改变系统、观察反馈、反复试探，才能搞清楚系统是怎么运作的——即“以行动求知”（act to know）。

方法与数据：作者构建了 EmbodiedLab。之所以选定量科学实验，是因为它既可控又可精确评分：每个实例的系统参数（如质量、摩擦、电路参数）都会重新随机采样，因此结果不可能提前背下来，但最终答案能严格判分。基准包含 5 个学科、14 种实验装置平台上的 30 个实验。智能体拿到任务目标和实验装置后，自己决定实验流程，在基于物理的仿真实验室里操作设备，并通过自身相机读取仪器示数。

评测方式：评分有两个维度——一是“它学到了什么”，依据是回合中实际记录到的仪器读数，防止它靠猜；二是任务要求的最终物理状态是否达成。所有实验都经过验证确保可解。

实验结果：作者在开发者自带的编程智能体框架中评测了 6 个前沿模型，设置三种条件：原生观测与控制、额外加入感知与运动规划模块、以及从最强智能体蒸馏得到的操作技能。结果显示：即便最强模型在原生的控制条件下成功率也不到一半；对所有智能体而言，失败大多发生在“与仪器交互”这一步，而不是推理；操作技能对弱模型的提升明显大于加感知模块带来的提升。

为何重要：它把“具身智能”的评测从“会不会动手完成任务”推进到“会不会动手搞明白事情”，并且用可精确判分的物理实验提供了严谨标尺。结论也给出明确方向：当前瓶颈不在高层推理，而在可靠地操作实验装置。
items.comment: Technical report. 19 pages, 10 figures, 9 tables. Project page: https://hexafuture.ai/benchmarks/embodiedlab/

rm.usage: 其“仿真实验室+通过相机读取仪表+每个实例可解性验证”的评测框架，可借鉴来搭建 sim 中自主任务的可解性与自评分机制（例如让哨兵在仿真里自主试错并记录有效读数）；但学科实验场景与 RM 任务差异大，需大量重写。

items.title_en: RynnVLA-Latent: Scaling Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models with 3D-Grounded Latent Actions
items.title_zh: RynnVLA-Latent：用三维接地的潜在动作扩展机器人操作基础模型
items.abstract_en: Scaling vision-language-action (VLA) models is constrained by scarce action-labeled demonstrations and incompatible control spaces across robot embodiments. We present RynnVLA-Latent, a framework that turns heterogeneous interaction videos into scalable supervision for robot policy pretraining. At its core, RynnLAM learns continuous, 3D-grounded latent actions from visual transitions without requiring native robot controls. By combining residual future-feature prediction, camera-compensated 3D-flow supervision, and camera-motion decoupling, RynnLAM encourages representations that capture control-relevant motion rather than appearance changes alone. We apply RynnLAM to 30.1K hours of human, robot, and simulation videos, producing 745.52M latent-action descriptors. RynnVLA-Latent then learns to predict latent-action chunks from visual observations and language through flow matching, before adapting its pretrained backbone and action expert to embodiment-specific robot actions. The resulting 4B policy achieves 98.8% success on LIBERO, 84.7% on LIBERO-Plus without benchmark-specific adaptation, 51.9% average success across five VLABench tracks, and 88.6% average success on the RoboTwin 2.0 bimanual benchmark. It also achieves the highest observed success rates among the compared methods on six real-world manipulation tasks across dexterous-hand and mobile-gripper platforms. Together with representation ablations and data-scaling results, these findings demonstrate the potential of latent-action supervision for scaling robot policy learning beyond native action-labeled data.
items.abstract_zh: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型的规模化受限于稀缺的动作标注演示数据，以及不同机器人本体之间互不兼容的控制空间。作者提出 RynnVLA-Latent 框架，把异构交互视频转化为可规模化的机器人策略预训练监督。其核心 RynnLAM 无需原生机器人控制信号，即可从视觉变化中学习连续、三维接地的潜在动作；它结合残差未来特征预测、相机补偿的三维光流监督与相机运动解耦，促使表征捕捉与操控相关的运动而非单纯外观变化。作者将 RynnLAM 应用于 30.1K 小时的人类、机器人与仿真视频，生成 7.4552 亿条潜在动作描述子。随后 RynnVLA-Latent 通过流匹配从视觉观测和语言预测潜在动作块，再将预训练主干与动作专家适配到具体本体的机器人动作。所得 4B 策略在 LIBERO 上达 98.8% 成功率，未经基准特定适配在 LIBERO-Plus 上达 84.7%，在 VLABench 五条赛道平均 51.9%，在 RoboTwin 2.0 双臂基准平均 88.6%；在灵巧手与移动夹爪平台上的六项真实操作任务中也取得所比较方法中最高的成功率。表征消融与数据规模化结果共同表明，潜在动作监督有望让机器人策略学习突破原生动作标注数据的限制。
items.highlight_zh: 从海量异构视频学三维接地潜在动作，突破动作标注瓶颈
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：机器人“视觉-语言-动作”大模型想做大，卡在两处：一是带动作标签的真实示教数据太贵太少；二是不同机器人的控制方式（关节数、夹爪类型）完全不同，难以共用一套动作空间。但互联网上有海量的人类操作视频、其他机器人视频和仿真视频，它们没有统一动作标签，却有丰富的“动作导致画面变化”的信息。

方法：作者提出 RynnVLA-Latent。核心组件 RynnLAM 不需要任何机器人的原始控制指令，而是从相邻帧的视觉变化中反推出连续的、带三维几何含义的“潜在动作”。为让学到的表征真正反映运动而不是外观，它用了三招：预测未来的残差特征、用相机补偿后的三维光流做监督、把相机自身运动与物体运动解耦。

规模：作者把 RynnLAM 跑在 30.1K 小时的人类、机器人与仿真视频上，产出约 7.4552 亿条潜在动作描述子。之后模型通过流匹配，从视觉观测和语言指令预测潜在动作块，最后把预训练主干与动作专家适配到具体机器人本体上输出真实控制。

结果：这个 4B 参数的策略在 LIBERO 上成功率 98.8%；不做任何基准特定适配就在 LIBERO-Plus 上达 84.7%；在 VLABench 五条赛道平均 51.9%；在双臂 RoboTwin 2.0 上平均 88.6%。在灵巧手与移动夹爪两类平台的六项真实操作任务中，其成功率也是对比方法中最高的。消融实验验证了三维光流监督与解耦设计的必要性，数据规模化实验显示随数据增多性能持续提升。

为何重要：它提供了一条“用无动作标签视频喂饱机器人模型”的可行路径——先把视频压缩成与本体无关的潜在动作，再迁移到真实机器人，从而绕开动作标注稀缺与本体不兼容这两大瓶颈。

rm.usage: 从无动作标注的示教视频学习潜在动作，可为工程机器人视觉装配（抓取42mm发射机构、能量单元）提供“用人类演示视频预训练操作策略”的思路，但4B模型与本体适配流程难以在车载算力上落地，只能作研究性参考。

items.title_en: RoboJev: An Open Vision-Language Judge for Robot Success Detection
items.title_zh: RoboJev：用于机器人任务成功检测的开放视觉语言评判器
items.abstract_en: Many robot manipulation videos do not indicate whether the task was successfully completed. RoboJev-27B is an open-weight vision-language model that takes a task instruction, 10 frames of a manipulation attempt, and (if available) final frames from auxiliary cameras and predicts whether the robot accomplished the task. RoboJev-27B is a variant of JEV-27B-VL, trained with a rank-32 LoRA adapter on the language model only (keeping the vision encoder frozen) using 52,598 episode records. It also uses a source-specific KL penalty that applies only to research data, anchoring predictions closer to the original model on those sources. It uses a calibrated two-token readout that outputs success/failure probabilities in a single forward pass. On 268 held-out episodes of the same robot model (SO-101), RoboJev-27B attains 95.2% balanced accuracy and 0.993 AUROC. It also generalises to episodes collected by unseen labs/robots (AUROC = 0.890 over 459 episodes) as well as to clearly labelled community-collected episodes (accuracy = 93.3% over 135 episodes), where the base model attains an AUROC = 0.900 on the unseen-lab/robot subset with the same inputs. It takes 0.26 seconds per episode (median, serial) to infer on a single H100, which is about \$0.19 per 1,000 success predictions at \$2.69 per GPU-hour (not including media processing and serving costs). RoboJev-27B is released together with its inference code, along with a transparent evaluation: 20,628 predictions organized into 29 model/protocol entries are made available to facilitate browsing and to enable reproducible benchmarking of success detection. We also compare against strong API-based frontier VLMs, which take in fewer input frames (4 images from the primary camera only); note that this comparison is not strictly like-for-like because RoboJev-27B is given more frames at inference.
items.abstract_zh: 许多机器人操作视频并不标明任务是否成功完成。RoboJev-27B 是一个开放权重的视觉语言模型，输入任务指令、一次操作尝试的 10 帧画面，以及（若有）辅助相机的末尾帧，即可预测机器人是否完成任务。它基于 JEV-27B-VL 改造，仅在语言模型部分加装 rank-32 LoRA 适配器（视觉编码器保持冻结），训练数据为 52,598 条回合记录；并采用只作用于研究数据来源的 KL 惩罚，使这些来源上的预测更贴近原模型。它使用校准的双 token 读出，在一次前向中输出成功/失败概率。在同一机器人型号（SO-101）的 268 条留出回合上，RoboJev-27B 取得 95.2% 平衡准确率与 0.993 AUROC；它还能泛化到未见过实验室/机器人采集的回合（459 条回合上 AUROC = 0.890）以及标注清晰的社区采集回合（135 条上准确率 93.3%）；在同一输入下，基座模型在未见实验室/机器人子集上的 AUROC 为 0.900。单张 H100 上串行推理每条回合中位耗时 0.26 秒，按每 GPU 小时 2.69 美元计，约合每千次成功预测 0.19 美元（不含媒体处理与服务成本）。作者同时发布推理代码，并给出透明评测：公开 20,628 条预测、组织为 29 个模型/协议条目，便于浏览与可复现的成功检测基准测试。文中还与强 API 前沿视觉语言模型作了比较，但后者输入帧更少（仅主相机 4 张图），该比较并非严格同条件。
items.highlight_zh: 开源 27B 视觉语言评判器，单次前向判别机器人任务成败
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：机器人操作视频大量存在，但绝大多数没有标注“这次抓取到底成功了没有”。人工逐条看视频打标签成本极高，而任务成功与否恰恰是评估策略、筛选训练数据、做自动回归测试时最基本的信息。

方法：作者发布 RoboJev-27B，一个开放权重的视觉语言模型评判器。输入是任务指令、该次操作尝试的 10 帧画面，如果有辅助相机还可以加上末尾帧；输出是任务成功或失败。模型基于已有的 JEV-27B-VL 改造，只在语言模型上加了 rank-32 的 LoRA 适配器，视觉编码器完全冻结，训练用了 52,598 条回合记录。它还加了一种只对研究数据来源生效的 KL 惩罚，让这些来源上的预测更贴近原模型，避免过拟合；输出端用经过校准的双 token 读出，一次前向即可给出成功/失败概率，而不需要多次采样或额外校准。

结果：在同一型号（SO-101）的 268 条留出回合上，平衡准确率 95.2%，AUROC 0.993；跨到未见过的实验室/机器人数据（459 条回合）AUROC 为 0.890，社区采集、标注清晰的 135 条回合上准确率 93.3%。作为对照，基座模型在同样输入下于未见实验室子集上 AUROC 为 0.900——说明泛化场景仍有提升空间。速度上，单张 H100 串行推理每条回合中位 0.26 秒，约合每千次预测 0.19 美元，且不含媒体处理与服务开销。

为何重要：它把“任务是否成功”的判定做成一个便宜、快速、可本地部署的开源组件，让大规模机器人视频数据能够自动打标，也为该任务提供了可复现的公开评测集（20,628 条预测、29 个模型/协议条目）。需要注意，与前沿 API 模型的对比并非严格同条件，因为对方只看了主相机的 4 帧。

rm.usage: 可作为一个离线工具，用比赛/训练录像自动判定某次操作（如工程装配、飞镖装填）是否成功，用于自动标注与回归评测；实时比赛环节用不上。

items.title_en: Intrinsic Goals for Autonomous Agents: Hierarchical Exploration Captures Future Volitional Action in Drosophila
items.title_zh: 自主智能体的内在目标：分层探索捕捉果蝇未来的意志性动作
items.abstract_en: Animals have a remarkable capacity for autonomy---driven by intrinsic motivation---without external sensory cues or extrinsic objectives, yet the computational mechanisms behind this ability largely remain a mystery. We combine whole-brain recordings in the fruit fly (Drosophila melanogaster), which reveal neural representations of spontaneous exploratory decisions more than 10 seconds in advance, with a neuromechanical digital twin to test whether optimizing intrinsic goals yields realistically embodied artificial agents that quantitatively match fly behavior and internal representations of future volitional action during exploration. Our hierarchical policy selects from a discrete library of low-level motor primitives, consistent with ethological theories of behavioral syllables. We train agents without external reward using 20 intrinsic motivation algorithms spanning curiosity, entropy, and competency methods. The agents are evaluated in a virtual tethered-ball assay modeled on the fly experiment, comparing spontaneous locomotor statistics and internal representations and decoding future turn direction from kinematics and neural activity on the same timescales observed in flies. DIAYN, a hierarchical competency algorithm learning discrete policies that maximize behavioral entropy and the separability of induced sensory observations, achieves the strongest joint behavioral and neural prospective coding performance relative to flies. Its learned policies closely capture individual variability in fly exploration strategies, suggesting that this diversity serves to maximize state-space coverage at the population level. DIAYN's latent activity also closely captures the sum-difference rule for interhemispheric encoding of kinematics in biological flies. These results establish hierarchical, intrinsically motivated agents as a powerful framework for reverse-engineering animal autonomy.
items.abstract_zh: 动物具备惊人的自主性，其驱动力来自内在动机，无需外部感觉线索或外在目标，但其背后的计算机制在很大程度上仍是谜。我们将果蝇（Drosophila melanogaster）全脑记录——该记录揭示自发探索决策在动作发生前10秒以上的神经表征——与神经力学数字孪生相结合，检验优化内在目标能否产生具身化的智能体，使其行为与探索时对未来意志性动作的内部表征在数量上与果蝇相匹配。我们的分层策略从离散的低层运动基元库中选择动作，这与关于行为“音节”的习性学理论一致。我们在无外部奖励条件下，用涵盖好奇心、熵与胜任力三类方法的20种内在动机算法训练智能体，并在仿照果蝇实验搭建的虚拟拴系球实验中评估其自发运动统计量，以及与果蝇相同时间尺度上从运动学和神经活动解码未来转向的能力。分层胜任力算法 DIAYN 学习最大化行为熵与感官观测可分性的离散策略，在行为与神经前瞻性编码两方面综合表现最接近果蝇。其学到的策略能再现果蝇探索策略的个体差异，提示这种多样性在群体层面用于最大化状态空间覆盖；其隐活动也符合真实果蝇半球间运动学编码的“和-差”规则。
items.highlight_zh: 内在动机算法 DIAYN 训练的具身智能体可定量复现果蝇的探索行为与神经预编码。
items.digest_zh:
【研究了什么问题】动物能在没有外部奖励、没有明确任务的情况下自发地探索世界，这种“自主性”从何而来一直是未解之谜。作者追问：如果让人工智能体只追求“内在目标”（好奇心、探索欲等），能否造出行为乃至大脑活动都像真实果蝇的智能体？

【用了什么方法】两条线结合。实验端用果蝇全脑成像，发现自发转向决策在动作真正发生前10秒以上就已被神经活动表征；建模端构建果蝇的“神经力学数字孪生”，把智能体放进仿照真实实验设计的虚拟拴系球场景。智能体采用分层策略：高层从一组离散的低层运动基元中挑选动作（对应习性学中“行为音节”的观点），并用20种内在动机算法在完全无外部奖励的条件下训练。

【有什么结果】在众多算法中，DIAYN（一种分层胜任力算法，鼓励策略最大化行为多样性、并让不同行为对应的感官输入易于区分）表现最好：它产生的自发运动统计量最接近果蝇，也能在相同时间尺度上从运动学预测未来的转向；其内部隐活动甚至重现了真实果蝇两半球间编码运动学的“和-差”规则。此外，不同个体智能体学到的策略差异，恰好对应果蝇个体间探索风格的差异。

【为何重要】这说明“内在动机”可能是自主性的一种可计算解释：不需要外部奖励，仅靠优化内在目标就能涌现出与生物高度相似的行为与神经表征。它也提供了一种新范式——用人工智能体反过来检验神经科学假说，并对机器人自主探索有直接启发。

rm.usage: 内在动机+分层离散动作基元的探索策略，理论上有助于 sim 中无奖励预训练哨兵探索行为，但果蝇神经科学设定与 RM 场景相距甚远，仅可作好奇心驱动 RL 的泛读参考。

items.title_en: $Ψ$-0.6: Adaptive Streams of Thought in a Unified Vision-Language World Model
items.title_zh: Ψ-0.6：统一视觉-语言世界模型中的自适应思维流
items.abstract_en: Humans reason about the physical world by flexibly combining different forms of inference as a problem unfolds. Achieving this flexibility is a major open challenge in AI: capabilities often remain separated across specialized models, limiting how they can be composed and jointly adapted to a task. We introduce $Ψ$-0.6, a unified vision-language world model that adaptively composes perception, language, geometry, and simulation within a shared reasoning process we call streams of thought. These streams interleave images, text, and explicit representations of geometry and motion, all of which the model can generate and interpret through a shared token interface. $Ψ$-0.6 surpasses leading open-weight models zero-shot on multi-view spatial reasoning, with further gains from reasoning through geometric intermediates. It also supports counterfactual simulation: generating and interpreting imagined scenes to determine, for example, whether moving an object would obstruct a pathway. Reinforcement learning from task feedback jointly optimizes the selection, generation, and use of intermediate representations, improving visual question-answering accuracy with gains that transfer to unseen benchmarks. $Ψ$-0.6 offers a path toward adaptive physical reasoning -- not only predicting the physical world but also choosing the representations through which to reason.
items.abstract_zh: 人类会随着问题的发展灵活组合不同的推理方式来理解物理世界。实现这种灵活性是人工智能的一大公开挑战：能力往往被分隔在各自的专用模型中，限制了它们的组合与针对任务的联合适配。我们提出 Ψ-0.6，一个统一的视觉-语言世界模型，它在被称为“思维流”的共享推理过程中自适应地组合感知、语言、几何与模拟。这些思维流交错包含图像、文本以及几何与运动的显式表示，模型可通过共享的 token 接口生成并解读它们。Ψ-0.6 在多视角空间推理上零样本超越领先的开源权重模型，并通过以几何中间量进行推理获得进一步提升。它还支持反事实模拟：生成并解读想象中的场景，例如判断移动某个物体是否会挡住通路。基于任务反馈的强化学习联合优化中间表示的选择、生成与使用，提升视觉问答准确率，且增益可迁移到未见基准。Ψ-0.6 为自适应物理推理开辟了道路——不仅预测物理世界，还能选择用何种表示来推理。
items.highlight_zh: 统一世界模型用“思维流”自适应组合感知、语言、几何与模拟来推理物理世界。
items.digest_zh:
【研究了什么问题】人类面对一个物理问题时，会随着问题展开灵活切换推理方式：有时看图，有时用语言描述，有时在脑中做几何推演或“如果……会怎样”的模拟。而现有 AI 的这些能力大多分散在不同的专用模型里，很难组合起来、共同适配到同一个任务上。

【用了什么方法】作者提出 Ψ-0.6，一个统一的视觉-语言“世界模型”。核心概念是“思维流”：在同一个推理过程里，模型自适应地把感知、语言、几何和模拟组合起来，流中交错着图像、文本以及几何与运动的显式表示，全部通过共享的 token 接口来生成和解读。作者还用基于任务反馈的强化学习，联合优化“选哪种中间表示、怎么生成、怎么使用”这几件事。

【有什么结果】在多视角空间推理任务上，Ψ-0.6 零样本就超过了领先的开源权重模型；如果让它先生成几何中间量再推理，成绩还能进一步提高。它还能做反事实模拟：生成并解读想象中的场景，比如判断把某个物体挪走会不会堵住通路。强化学习带来的视觉问答准确率提升，也能迁移到训练时没见过的基准上。

【为何重要】这项工作的意义不只是“更准地预测物理世界”，而是让模型学会选择用哪种表示来思考——就像人会在画图、算数和心象模拟之间切换。这是迈向自适应物理推理的一步，对未来能灵活解决真实场景问题的具身智能与通用模型都有启示。

rm.usage: 世界模型中的反事实推演（若某物体移动是否阻断通路）思路可类比到 strategy 的战术推演或 sim 中的对抗态势预测，但模型规模与推理成本决定了不能在赛场上实时使用。

items.title_en: Learning Scene Coordinate Reconstruction from Unposed Images via Pose Graph Optimization
items.title_zh: 通过位姿图优化从无位姿图像学习场景坐标重建
items.abstract_en: Learning-based structure-from-motion methods such as ACE-Zero have demonstrated strong performance in estimating cameraposes and scene coordinates from unordered image collections without requiring ground truth supervision. However, the lack of global and multi-view consistency constraints in ACE-Zero can lead to pose drift and misalignment, particularly in complex or ambiguous scenes. In this work, we propose a hybrid framework that integrates pose graph optimization (PGO) into ACE-Zero to refine camera poses and suppress incorrect refinements. We construct pose graphs directly from ACE-Zero outputs by extracting relative pose constraints from predicted scene coordinates. Furthermore, we introduce an uncertainty-aware optimization strategy by estimating confidence scores using geometric priors, including epipolar and optical flow consistencies across views. Our approach improves the robustness and accuracy of pose estimation, demonstrating that global geometric reasoning can effectively complement learning-based inference in structure-from-motion.

rm.usage: 用无位姿图像重建场景坐标并用位姿图优化抑制漂移，可用于赛前对场地拍摄图像做重建、生成场景坐标先验，供哨兵/雷达做重定位与地图校正，提升长时运行的位姿一致性。

items.title_en: SAGE: Semantic-Augmented Geometric Experts for Point Cloud Registration
items.title_zh: SAGE：用于点云配准的语义增强几何专家
items.abstract_en: Point cloud registration is an essential task for scene reconstruction, requiring the alignment of partially overlapping point clouds. Under low-overlap conditions, this task remains challenging because existing geometry-only methods cannot distinguish geometrically similar but semantically distinct structures (e.g., TV corners vs. desk corners and chair legs vs. table legs), resulting in incorrect correspondences. To address this geometric ambiguity, we present Semantic-Augmented Geometric Experts (SAGE), which integrates frozen pre-trained point cloud semantic representations into the registration pipeline without requiring additional sensors or fine-tuning the semantic encoder. To effectively leverage these semantic distinctions, SAGE employs a Semantic-Guided Mixture of Experts (SG-MoE) architecture. Through semantic-aware routing, SG-MoE enables each expert to specialize in distinct semantic-geometric patterns, reducing mismatches that confound geometry-only methods. With a structure-aware estimator, SAGE achieves the highest registration recall on 3DLoMatch while remaining competitive on 3DMatch. When evaluated with the same number of refinement iterations, SAGE further achieves the highest inlier ratio and registration recall on both benchmarks. These results indicate that frozen semantic representations provide effective cues for resolving geometric ambiguity in low-overlap registration.

rm.usage: 语义增强的点云配准在低重叠下更鲁棒，可用于哨兵激光雷达的里程计/重定位，或在雷达端做多视角点云配准与标定，避免几何相似结构（如场地护栏与立柱）造成的错误匹配。

items.title_en: SVIn+: Multi-Modal Framework for Robust Underwater State Estimation using 3D Sonar, Visual-Inertial, Water-Pressure, and DVL
items.title_zh: SVIn+：使用3D声纳、视觉惯性、水压和DVL的鲁棒水下状态估计多模态框架
items.abstract_en: As expansion and scalability in underwater oper- ations becomes more important and challenging, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) become more relevant and the necessity for reliable autonomy more critical. A fundamental challenge in any autonomous underwater operation, from control to safe navigation and mapping, is state estimation; a notorious hard problem to address, especially in low visibility conditions. In this paper, we tackle this problem, by presenting SVIn+, a multi-sensor framework for robust state estimation of AUVs equipped with an IMU, cameras, a water-pressure sensor, a Doppler Velocity Log (DVL), and a compact 3D sonar. This framework extends an established open-source state-of-the-art visual-inertial SLAM, SVIn, by integrating water-pressure and DVL measurements into a tightly-coupled nonlinear optimiza- tion formulation resulting in improved estimates. To leverage the structural information of recently available 3D acoustic sonars while maintaining computational efficiency, we introduce a hierarchical architecture that incorporates estimates from a decoupled front-end via KISS-ICP, treated as relative pose factors within the factor graph. The proposed framework is validated through field deployments in a shipwreck and coral reef, demonstrating drift mitigation and global consistency. To support further research in underwater multi-modal fusion, the code and the datasets can be found on project website https://cmburgul.github.io/projects/svin+/ https://dartmouthrobotics.github.io/svin-plus

rm.usage: 水下多模态状态估计与RM地面机器人传感器配置差异很大，关联很弱；仅其多源融合框架可作哨兵定位的泛化参考，实用价值有限。

items.title_en: UT-HMR: Uncertainty-Guided Temporal Modeling for Robust 3D Human Mesh Recovery
items.title_zh: UT-HMR：面向鲁棒3D人体网格恢复的不确定性引导时序建模
items.abstract_en: Monocular 3D human mesh recovery (HMR) remains unreliable under weak observations caused by long camera-to-person distances, occlusion, and motion blur. In challenging scenarios such as sports, these factors make the problem highly ambiguous, as different 3D poses may yield similar 2D projections. This ambiguity is especially severe for one-stage HMR, which recovers all meshes directly from the full image without person crops or external 2D cues. To handle this ambiguity, we present UT-HMR ( Uncertainty-guided Temporal HMR), to our knowledge the first one-stage HMR framework to capture correlated pose uncertainty across joints. Each person query predicts a Gaussian distribution over the full SMPL pose with a compact low-rank-plus-diagonal covariance, which is converted into joint-wise precision weights for heteroscedastic supervision while keeping inference deterministic. Temporal early fusion further injects neighboring-frame evidence before pose decoding, supplying the visual evidence needed to resolve the ambiguity that the uncertainty captures. With a lightweight ViT-B backbone, UT-HMR achieves state-of-the-art results on VIP-HockeyPose-v2 (ice hockey) and WorldPose (soccer), reducing MPJPE, PA-MPJPE, and PVE by up to 4.7%, 3.8%, and 5.6%, and remains competitive on 3DPW against methods with larger backbones and higher input resolutions.

rm.usage: 面向人体3D网格恢复，RM自瞄与感知目标是装甲板、能量机关和机器人，不涉及人体姿态，基本用不上。

items.title_en: Closed-Loop Aware Planning via Imitation-Free Speed Scoring for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
items.title_zh: 面向端到端自动驾驶的基于无模仿速度评分的闭环感知规划
items.abstract_en: End-to-end autonomous driving has predominantly relied on open-loop imitation learning for training, which presents two limitations. First, expert demonstrations show only one behavior per scenario, so the model cannot learn alternative valid behaviors and, in turn, cannot adapt to user-specified preferences at test time. Second, noise or ambiguity in these demonstrations can produce inconsistent, unreliable supervision for the end-to-end models. Driving is inherently multi-modal: multiple different behaviors can be valid responses to the same scene, and this diversity arises largely from speed rather than path. We introduce a planning paradigm that learns the path through imitation while scoring a set of candidate speeds across multiple criteria with a learned function supervised by physically grounded safety constraints. We realize this paradigm as Closed-Loop Aware Planning for Autonomous Driving (CLAP-AD), a plug-in planning head that integrates with existing end-to-end driving models and, to our knowledge, is the first to enable explicit test-time control over their speed selection without speed-conditioned training. On Bench2Drive-Speed, CLAP-AD sets a new state of the art Speed-Adherence Score of 82.53, topping TFv6, the strongest baseline on this metric, by 12.9 points while retaining strong closed-loop driving performance. On Bench2Drive, it improves driving score by +28.5 and +32.7 over UniAD and VAD, and on NAVSIM v2, built on real-world driving data, EPDMS by +6.1 over its backbone. Project page: https://clap-ad.github.io

items.title_en: Revisiting Direct Control: A Field Evaluation of Sensor Fusion Efficacy in Teleoperating Full-Scale Autonomous Vehicles via Bird's Eye View
items.title_zh: 重新审视直接控制：通过鸟瞰图遥操作全尺寸自动驾驶车辆中传感器融合效能的现场评估
items.abstract_en: In autonomous driving, robot teleoperation serves as a critical safety fallback mechanism, requiring operators to assume direct control in the event of system failure. While recent research has pivoted toward high-level supervisory control or simulation-based studies, these approaches often fail to capture the physical dynamics and sensory demands of driving a full-scale vehicle. To address this gap, we evaluated the impact of spatial data representation on operator performance using a real car-sized vehicle in a field experiment with $N = 18$ participants. We compared three visualization interfaces: (i) a standard camera feed baseline, with two bird's-eye views (BEV) from (ii) a raw LiDAR point cloud, and (iii) a sensor fusion of LiDAR and camera data streams. Contrary to prior passive observation studies suggesting that sensor-fusion BEV may hinder awareness, our active-control results demonstrate that such representation significantly outperforms the standard LiDAR BEV in perceived usability ($p \leq 0.0001$) and cognitive task load ($p = 0.01$, NASA-TLX score: 34.58/100) while also being significantly better than the Camera-only view ($p = 0.043$). The fused interface also led to statistically significant reductions in task completion time ($p = 0.0461$) and superior usability (SUS: 77.9/100) compared to those of the Camera-only and LiDAR-only views. By synthesizing objective performance data with comprehensive subjective assessments, we demonstrate that BEV fusion maximizes safety margins while minimizing the operator's mental demand. These findings challenge existing teleoperation conventions and provide an empirically validated approach for designing robust remote piloting systems.

items.title_en: Sparse Recovery Bird's-Eye View Model Soup for Robust Camera-Based 3D Object Detection
items.title_zh: 用于鲁棒相机3D目标检测的稀疏恢复鸟瞰图Model Soup
items.abstract_en: Camera-based bird's-eye view (BEV) perception methods such as Fast-BEV have demonstrated promising results with fast inference speed and competitive accuracy. However, their robustness to real-world corruptions remains insufficiently explored, posing risks for autonomous driving deployment where environmental variations are inevitable. In this paper, we propose Sparse Recovery Bird's-Eye View Model Soup (SR-BEVS), a sparse recovery learning approach that simultaneously improves clean accuracy and corruption robustness without requiring additional data or architectural modifications. Our method identifies pruning candidates based on layer-wise weight magnitudes, applies random pruning to create diverse sparse models, and retrains each model with a randomly sampled learning rate. By averaging these diverse recovered models into a single dense model, we achieve enhanced robustness against various corruptions while introducing zero inference overhead. We further provide a mode connectivity analysis demonstrating that our pruning-based diversification preserves the connected low-loss basin necessary for stable weight averaging. Experiments on the nuScenes dataset demonstrate up to 33.8% improvement in corruption robustness and a 1.8% gain in clean accuracy over the Fast-BEV baseline, with consistent improvements across sensor noise, weather distortions, and illumination changes. Our simple yet effective approach may be applicable to other BEV models.

items.title_en: AdaDexTrack: Dynamic Modulation for Adaptive and Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation Tracking
items.title_zh: AdaDexTrack：面向自适应与可泛化灵巧操作跟踪的动态调制
items.abstract_en: Language is a natural way to command robots, but converting a single instruction into a long-horizon, contact-rich hand-object interaction remains challenging: synthesized references are noisy, human-to-robot retargeting introduces embodiment bias, and fixed-reference tracking lets small errors snowball. We address this with AdaDexTrack, a modulator-in-the-loop framework for language-conditioned manipulation tracking. A distilled generalist tracker serves as the skill carrier, while a tightly aligned modulator performs three feedback corrections: reference modulation (continual adjustment of what to track), object-latent modulation (online adaptation of the object representation to recruit suitable skills), and positional-target modulation (small state-dependent refinements for execution). The tracker is learned via large-scale specialist to generalist distillation on a corpus of language-conditioned hand-object trajectories; the modulator is trained with RL under the same task objective, ensuring tight coupling. Across large-scale evaluations, AdaDexTrack consistently outperforms prior SOTA on unseen-trajectory and unseen-object sets in both average tracking error and success rate, demonstrating robustness and generalization. We further show zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on real hardware, where adding the modulator yields substantial gains over a tracker-only variant. AdaDexTrack reframes language-conditioned dexterous manipulation as modulated tracking, replacing the open-loop, fixed-reference tracking with in-loop modulation that adjusts the reference, object latent, and positional target, yielding drift-resistant execution from noisy text references.
items.comment: CVPR 2026. 18 pages, 14 figures, including supplementary material. Project page: https://janebek.github.io/AdaDexTrack/

items.title_en: HIDRA: Hierarchical Dual-Routing Attention for Replay-Free Lifelong Imitation Learning
items.title_zh: HIDRA：用于无回放终身模仿学习的分层双路由注意力
items.abstract_en: Robotic agents operating in real-world environments must adapt continuously from a stream of multimodal demonstrations, often under constraints that preclude storing or revisiting past data. In this replay-free, single-pass lifelong imitation learning setting, sequential updates can progressively distort the representation space, making expert-based approaches particularly sensitive to routing interference, causing expert selection to degrade over time. We propose HIDRA, a structured routing framework that mitigates this issue through a hierarchical dual-attention mechanism, which decouples instruction-level expert retrieval from context-dependent refinement. To further stabilize routing under representation drift, HIDRA introduces a key-level geometric regularization that enforces both alignment within tasks and separation across tasks. The resulting approach enables reliable expert selection while supporting an expandable set of experts for continual adaptation. We evaluate HIDRA on several LIBERO benchmark suites, including more challenging variants with heterogeneous task sequences and paraphrased language instructions. Our approach consistently outperforms both replay-free and replay-based baselines, improving AUC and forward transfer while maintaining low forgetting, with stronger gains under high interference and language variation. The code is available at: https://github.com/yfqi/HIDRA.
items.comment: This is the authors' preprint, accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 Conference. The final version is available in the NeurIPS 2026 proceedings

items.title_en: Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Using Routed Ensembles and Trajectory Attribution
items.title_zh: 使用路由集成与轨迹归因的多目标强化学习
items.abstract_en: Multi-objective reinforcement learning is a fundamental problem for modern AI, with applications spanning post-training, reasoning models, and robotic control. A central challenge is to learn policies that balance competing objectives, such as helpfulness versus honesty in safety and alignment, or speed versus energy in robotics. The optimal policy can vary sharply with objective-weighting combinations, and the extent of this variation depends crucially on the degree of conflict among objectives, making per-preference policy learning sample-inefficient. In this paper, we introduce objective-conflict coefficients and derive near-optimal regret bounds for online settings using this measure, thereby quantifying the impact of misalignment on learning efficiency. Then, we design routed ensemble policy learning, an algorithm that maintains a small set of basis policies and dynamically routes trajectories to the policy with the highest potential reward. Finally, we consider trajectory selection as another approach to mitigate objective conflict, and design a kernel surrogate trajectory attribution algorithm that estimates how feedback signals from a set of trajectories influence policy learning on other trajectories. The kernel can capture nonlinear interactions such as synergy and antagonism between trajectories. We evaluate our approach across diverse environments and benchmarks: routed ensembles improve average performance by 4.3% over baselines for online environments from Meta-World and MO-Gymnasium, and kernel surrogate attribution improves correlation with leave-one-out analysis over existing baselines by 50%. When applied to trajectory selection, kernel-based attribution yields a 27% improvement in reward over baseline attribution methods.
items.comment: 30 pages. To appear at NeurIPS 2026 (extended version)

items.title_en: SO-101 Bench: Accessible Spatial Manipulation
items.title_zh: SO-101 Bench：易用的空间操作
items.abstract_en: Low-cost arms such as the SO-101 have become the most common entry point to robot learning, yet no released policy performs spatially constrained, language-conditioned tasks on them out of the box, and existing SO-101 benchmarks run only on physical hardware with simple tasks and few held-out objects. We introduce SO-101 Bench, a simulated benchmark for language-conditioned spatial manipulation built on an Isaac Lab digital twin of a real SO-101 setup. It has four tasks scored as five families, 138 objects in seen, unseen-instance and unseen-class splits, 916 evaluation episodes with subsets for held-out appearances, rotate-to-fit planning and occlusion memory, and 3,629 simulated demonstrations on which every learned policy is fine-tuned under an equal compute budget. The twin ranks policies as the real robot does: five policies trained without real data, four VLAs and an LLM agent, keep their exact ranking when the same weights run on the physical arm in an unseen environment with unseen objects (Spearman rho = 1.00, MMRV = 0.000), although simulation overestimates success. Across nine VLAs and world-action models, the best learned policies score near 61%, with spatial placement, unseen object classes and rotate-to-fit planning remaining open. An LLM agent that writes code and hands grasping to a learned policy scores 83.2%, and an ablation shows that this lead comes from the choice of harness and the choice of language model.

items.title_en: Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor Critic for Decentralized LLM Collaboration
items.title_zh: 面向去中心化LLM协作的信念条件化多智能体Actor-Critic
items.abstract_en: Recent work has explored optimizing LLM collaboration through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), but many approaches still rely on predefined workflows, limiting efficiency and scalability. Decentralized LLM collaboration is challenging because agents execute independently with limited communication, share a joint objective, and must infer useful information from communication traces. In this paper, we propose BCMAAC, a Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor-Critic method that maintains beliefs over contextual information and uses them to facilitate training. Experiments on Minecraft game-playing, web searching and tool-using tasks show that BCMAAC improves task performance and collaborative behavior compared to naive actor-critic baselines. The improvements are particularly pronounced in multi-turn tasks with richer contextual information, where belief modeling provides a clear advantage.
items.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop PTA: From Pretrained Representations to Acting Agents. 18 pages, 3 figures

items.title_en: PosePlaner: Denoising Any Feed-Forward Pose Predictor from Pairwise Planar Geometry
items.title_zh: PosePlaner：基于成对平面几何对任意前馈位姿预测器进行去噪
items.abstract_en: Recent multi-view Transformers (e.g., DUSt3R and VGGT) have advanced 3D reconstruction by scaling training data and model capacity from two views to many views and long sequences, subsuming the classical SfM/SLAM pipeline of feature extraction, matching, and pose estimation in a single feed-forward pass. Yet this subsumption hides the interfaces between pipeline stages---correspondences, geometry, and pose are entangled in a single forward pass, leaving supervised fine-tuning as the major path to improvement and offering no mechanism to correct predictions from geometric evidence at test time. We propose PosePlaner to close this gap by reviving the classical coupling between correspondences and pose via flow matching, treating pose refinement as a conditional generation problem that takes coarse geometric matches and initial pose as input condition and fuses the resulting pose hypotheses into a single refined estimate, providing a continuous, data-driven analog of RANSAC voting. Our method is trained efficiently on two-view data, yet serves as a periodic refiner for streaming n-view pose estimators with no retraining. Empirically, it corrects failures of feed-forward predictors, substantially improves correspondence-based solvers, and reduces accumulated drift in long streaming sequences.

items.title_en: UniQuery: Unifying Vision Models with a Joint Query Head for Cross-Domain Pedestrian Attribute Recognition
items.title_zh: UniQuery：用联合查询头统一视觉模型以进行跨域行人属性识别
items.abstract_en: Pedestrian Attribute Recognition (PAR) predicts semantic attributes of individuals, such as gender, age, clothing and accessories, and its descriptions support attribute-based person retrieval and person re-identification. However, accurately recognizing fine-grained attributes across domains remains challenging due to occlusion, appearance variations, and shifts in image distributions. Ensembles of independently trained foundation encoders combine their logits with fixed fusion weights, so every attribute uses the same mix and the encoders are never trained together. We propose UniQuery, which instead jointly fine-tunes DINOv3 and CLIP for attribute-specific fusion. It combines two query heads, one for each encoder, with a joint query head whose attribute queries attend to tokens from both encoders, and the prediction is the average of the logits of the three query heads. We evaluate UniQuery on the benchmark of the UPAR Challenge 2027 at the WACV 2027 Real-World Surveillance workshop, where models are trained on PA100k, PETA and Market-1501 with a shared set of attributes. In leave-one-dataset-out experiments, UniQuery outperforms the independent ensemble in Challenge_Avg on both held-out datasets. Ablations show that learning fusion over independently trained encoders does not improve upon logit averaging in the mean over the two held-out datasets, while freezing the encoders lowers the Challenge_Avg of UniQuery. On the hidden test set of the benchmark, UniQuery achieves a Challenge_Avg of 0.8001.
items.comment: 10 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to the 7th Real-World Surveillance Workshop (RWS) at WACV 2027

items.title_en: Models Verify Sufficiency, Not Validity: Usable Falsehoods Evade the Checks that Gaps Trigger
items.title_zh: 模型验证的是充分性而非有效性：可用的虚假内容会规避缺口触发的检查
items.abstract_en: Ask a model "how many settlements did the Normans control?" and it answers that the passage does not say. Tell it "given that the Normans controlled 12 settlements of 400 inhabitants, what is the total?" and it computes 4,800. Nothing was added to the passage; the unsupported fact merely became usable. Benchmarks for unanswerable questions are built almost entirely by omission, deleting the fact a question needs and scoring refusal, so they never probe this. Holding source support fixed and varying only whether an unsupported premise is usable, flagging drops 8-30 points and commitment to an answer rises 1.5-2.3x on GSM8K across four models spanning two families and 2B-26B; all 16 paired contrasts remain significant after Holm correction. Two further manipulations reproduce it, one also on SQuAD: a fact asserted rather than asked about, and a corrupted intermediate value rather than a removed one. Models articulate the exact gap they then ignore, stating that "there is no financial information provided" for an inert premise and silently adopting a fabricated price for the same item. We read these as one behaviour: whether a model checks depends substantially on whether usable material is present, even when source support is held fixed. Because the main design never instructs models to reject premises introduced in the question, adopting such a premise can also be read as conditional reasoning, and we delimit what the design does and does not show. In the judging seat the pattern differs: asked whether the answer follows, judges pass solutions with a required step deleted 78-99% of the time at every scale tested. A natural prompt-level mitigation lowers accuracy by 22 points without improving detection.
items.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Self-Evolving Diversity-Driven Search for Robust AI Systems (EvoRobust). 5 pages plus references, 3 tables

items.title_en: Bracketing Shows the Way: Adaptive Multi-Exposure Policy as Input for Robust Visual SLAM
items.title_zh: 包围曝光指明方向：自适应多曝光策略作为鲁棒视觉SLAM的输入
items.abstract_en: Rapid illumination transitions can disturb Visual SLAM (VSLAM) by saturating images before the Automatic Exposure (AE) policy adapts, removing the visual correspondences needed to maintain tracking. Our proposed methods mitigate this disturbance at two levels: B-Adapt acquires adaptive exposure brackets to cover the scene dynamic range while promoting photometric overlap, and BVSLAM directly uses the multi-exposure sequence as constraints in a factor graph state estimator without relying on High Dynamic Range (HDR) merging. We evaluate both methods against state-of-the-art approaches in nominal environments and during a repeated tunnel-exit transition at an emulated vehicle speed of 32 m s-1. In the tunnel, combining our B-Adapt with BVSLAM reduces the state estimation error by 78 % compared with AE images. These results suggest that bracketing efficiently improves visual pose estimation robustness to rapid illumination disturbances while retaining low error under nominal conditions. Our code is available at https://github.com/norlab-ulaval/bracketing-shows-the-way.
items.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, submitted to 2027 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA 2027)

items.title_en: DriveOSS: Dataset and Benchmark for 3D Anomaly Segmentation and Open-set Semantic Segmentation in Autonomous Driving
items.title_zh: DriveOSS：自动驾驶中3D异常分割与开放集语义分割的数据集与基准
items.abstract_en: Recent advances in 3D semantic segmentation have significantly improved scene understanding in autonomous driving. However, existing methods are typically developed under a closed-set assumption and evaluated under standard driving conditions, where all categories are known in advance. In real-world driving, autonomous vehicles inevitably encounter previously unseen objects, making closed-set perception insufficient for safe deployment. To address this challenge, we introduce DriveOSS, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first real-world multimodal dataset and benchmark specifically designed for 3D anomaly segmentation and open-set semantic segmentation. It contains 12,661 synchronized and annotated frames captured using six surround-view RGB cameras, a 128-beam LiDAR, and a GPS/IMU unit. The dataset comprises 52 real-world driving scenes collected under clear, nighttime, cloudy, rainy, and snowy conditions and is organized into ID (in-distribution) and OOD (out-of-distribution) subsets. The ID scenes contain only known classes and are used for training, whereas the OOD scenes additionally contain unknown objects annotated as the outlier class and are used for validation and testing. Extensive experiments show that unseen objects remain a major challenge for current 3D perception systems. The dataset, benchmark protocols, and code are available at https://github.com/chrisyan/DriveOSS.

items.title_en: VERA-Hand: A Verified Multidimensional Benchmark for 2D Hand Pose Estimation in Third-Person Dynamic Gesture Videos
items.title_zh: VERA-Hand：用于第三人称动态手势视频中2D手部位姿估计的经校验多维基准
items.abstract_en: Hand landmarks serve as input for gesture recognition, sign language understanding, and touchless human-computer interaction. Yet hand pose estimators are typically evaluated with frame-wise localization metrics such as PCK or MPJPE, which are computed over matched predictions and overlook missed or spurious hands, handedness errors, and temporal instability. To address these limitations, we present VERA-Hand, a benchmark that evaluates estimators using manually verified, frame-level 2D annotations for 10,690 hands across four complementary dimensions (detection, localization, identification, and temporal stability), as well as a joint Pose-F1 metric that requires both correct detection and accurate localization. Evaluating six estimators spanning hand-specific, whole-body, reconstruction-based, and foundation-model paradigms, we find that no estimator dominates: rankings reorder sharply across dimensions. VERA-Hand also exposes failures that localization-only and downstream evaluations may not reveal, including cross-hand overlap in over 85% of frames for a recent foundation model. A post-hoc cleanup case study demonstrates how the benchmark can validate corrective interventions, while stratified analyses show that robustness varies across motion-blur classes and hand regions. We release the verified annotations, protocol, and code at https://gibranbenitez.github.io/VERA_Hand/

items.title_en: Hyperparameter and Neural Architecture Search via Evolutionary Optimization for Reinforcement Learning: HPNAS-RL
items.title_zh: 基于进化优化的强化学习超参数与神经架构搜索：HPNAS-RL
items.abstract_en: In this study, we propose a dual-branch evolutionary framework that simultaneously performs Neural Architecture Search (NAS) and Hyperparameter Optimization (HPO) for Reinforcement Learning (RL) in Autonomous Driving (AD) tasks. While NAS has shown strong potential in automating architecture design for Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), its application to RL remains limited, especially in scenarios that require joint optimization of architectural and training dynamics. Building on our prior work on Evolutionary Multi-Objective NAS (EMNAS), the proposed framework evolves discrete network architectures and continuous hyperparameters in parallel under a unified multi-objective search strategy. In this setup, NAS targets the convolutional layers of the RL policy network - responsible for visual feature extraction, while HPO focuses on optimizing critical RL hyperparameters. To accelerate convergence and improve generalization, we incorporate parallel evaluation and a teacher-student policy transfer mechanism. Experiments in a high-fidelity driving simulator show that the joint NAS-HPO framework consistently outperforms standalone NAS, yielding policies with higher rewards, fewer parameters, and improved stability. These results highlight the benefits of jointly optimizing model structure and training dynamics for scalable and effective RL agent design.

items.title_en: HoloRecon: Incremental Reconstruction of Long-Range Panoramas with Global Consistency
items.title_zh: HoloRecon：具有全局一致性的长距离全景图增量重建
items.abstract_en: Long-sequence panoramic reconstruction requires detailed scene geometry and globally consistent camera poses across distant revisits. Panoramic SLAM and incremental SfM rely on feature correspondences, but repeated, similar structures and small partial overlap make reliable long-range connections difficult to establish, leaving accumulated drift unresolved. Feed-forward models offer detailed local geometry, but their high computational costs limit inference window size, necessitating additional constraints for global consistency. This motivates combining continuous feature-based tracking and sparse mapping with rapid, high-quality local reconstruction from feed-forward models to achieve accurate localization and globally consistent dense mapping over long sequences. We therefore propose a panoramic reconstruction framework that couples an ORB-based sparse panoramic mapping frontend with a fine-tuned feed-forward model. Our key insight is that predicted local geometry enables 3D verification of feature matches across distant revisits, yielding long-range camera constraints even between regions. We calibrate predicted depths with sparse landmarks and use verified connections to optimize the global pose graph, updating dense geometry with the corrected camera poses. We also introduce PanoRecon, a seven-scene benchmark with repetitive architecture, large and small loops, and reference camera poses and LiDAR geometry for evaluating global consistency. Our method achieves the lowest mean absolute trajectory error and high F-1 Score among the evaluated methods. Project Page:https://zhuoxiaoli.github.io/HoloRecon_page/

items.title_en: ActiveAlign: Aligning Egocentric Manipulation via Active Perception
items.title_zh: ActiveAlign：通过主动感知对齐第一人称操作
items.abstract_en: Real-to-Sim-to-Real (Real2Sim2Real) enables structured world representations for planning, interpretability, and safe execution. Most existing approaches rely on passive perception, which creates real2sim gaps due to imperfect observation. Inspired by how humans perceive actively through actions, we propose ActiveAlign, a framework that leverages active perception to align the Real2Sim2Real gap from interactions. ActiveAlign introduces two complementary modules: (i) ActiveAlign-Waving, which performs hand-eye calibration by exploiting active hand motions and differentiable rendering, and (ii) ActiveAlign-Touching, which refines object alignment through tactile feedback to achieve millimeter-level precision. Together, these capabilities enable strong real2sim alignment. We demonstrate that ActiveAlign-Waving can be used to curate simulation environments for open-sourced uncalibrated robot manipulation datasets, and demonstrate on a real Unitree G1 robot that ActiveAlign enables fine manipulation of millimeter-scale objects such as pressing buttons and moving sliders.

items.title_en: LingGS: Decoupling Feed-Forward Geometry Prediction from Camera Tracking for High-Fidelity Gaussian SLAM
items.title_zh: LingGS：将前馈几何预测与相机跟踪解耦以实现高保真高斯SLAM
items.abstract_en: Achieving high-quality reconstruction and responsive camera tracking remains challenging for monocular RGB Gaussian splatting SLAM under a limited optimization budget. We present an online system that addresses this challenge by combining learned geometric priors with explicit geometric camera tracking, which can substantially outperform learned camera prediction in terms of tracking accuracy. A frozen streaming 3D foundation model serves as a virtual RGB-D sensor, providing depth estimation from monocular video. An explicit geometric solver then estimates camera motion through feature reprojection, and a streaming Gaussian mapper integrates the resulting observations into a dense scene representation. We further show that geometric tracking improves camera pose accuracy across representative streaming geometry backbones, demonstrating the broader applicability of our approach. Extensive experiments on indoor and outdoor datasets show that our method significantly improves reconstruction quality over existing approaches, achieving about 7 FPS on a single RTX 4090 and delivering 2-3 times the throughput of the evaluated prior SLAM systems.

items.title_en: When All Rollouts Fail: Policy-Compatible Joint Decoding for Hard-Problem Reasoning
items.title_zh: 当所有推演均失败时：面向难题推理的策略兼容联合解码
items.abstract_en: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) derives its learning signal from binary rewards via on-policy exploration and becomes a powerful paradigm for improving the reasoning of large language models. Yet it faces a learning cliff on problems beyond model's current ability: when every rollout fails, the samples reveal nothing about a correct solution, and group-relative estimators (e.g., GRPO, RLOO) collapse the update to zero advantage. Expert trajectories offer a remedy, but they are incompatible with the current policy and often lie in the student's low-probability regions, so the surviving updates demand large parameter shifts and decay into surface-level imitation rather than transferable reasoning. We argue that a useful learning signal on hard problems must be both verifiably correct and sufficiently compatible with the current policy. We propose Policy-Compatible Reinforcement Learning (PICO), which performs distribution-constrained joint decoding: expert data guides decoding at the token level while preserving the student's relative token probabilities, and a dynamic top-k mechanism confines the sampling distribution under a finite divergence budget, yielding trajectories that are verified and policy-compatible by construction. These trajectories are optimized jointly with on-policy rollouts under a mixed-behavior objective that mitigates their distribution mismatch via importance sampling. Experiments across reasoning diverse datasets and agentic benchmarks demonstrate that PICO consistently outperforms standard RLVR and prior off-policy baselines.

items.title_en: Trace-WAM: Learning to Act via 3D Motion Prediction for World Action Models
items.title_zh: Trace-WAM：面向世界动作模型，通过3D运动预测学习行动
items.abstract_en: World Action Models (WAMs) learn representations for robot control by coupling future visual prediction with action generation. Successful manipulation depends primarily on how the robot and task-relevant objects evolve, whereas future-video prediction must also reconstruct the appearance and background of the entire scene. We therefore propose Trace-WAM, which augments video-action learning with future 3D motion prediction as an auxiliary objective. This objective supervises temporal point correspondence together with image-plane displacement and depth change, directly describing the interaction dynamics and spatial changes involved in manipulation. To this end, we adopt a three-branch Mixture-of-Transformer (Tri-MoT) architecture to jointly learn video prediction, motion prediction, and action generation. The motion expert predicts future trajectories from current visual features, allowing motion supervision to shape the representations used for action generation. Because the action expert does not consume predicted trajectories, inference retains the current-observation policy path: a single visual forward pass followed by action denoising. Experiments on RoboCasa-GR1, LIBERO, and LIBERO-Plus demonstrate strong in-distribution performance and out-of-distribution generalization, with particularly clear gains over Fast-WAM under limited demonstrations and distribution shifts.

rm.usage: 世界动作模型中的3D运动预测可作为工程机器人装配/操作策略学习的辅助目标，也可在仿真中构建面向操作的世界模型；对RM其他环节帮助有限。

items.title_en: SetGRPO: Calibrating Grader-Induced Policy Optimization
items.title_zh: SetGRPO：校准评分器诱导的策略优化
items.abstract_en: Rubric-based reinforcement learning uses fine-grained grader feedback to train large language models on open-ended tasks, but grader randomness can alter GRPO updates in ways that score discrepancies alone cannot characterize. Because GRPO jointly normalizes rewards within each response group and combines the resulting training coefficients with response-level gradients, a scoring discrepancy can shift the coefficients of the entire group and induce policy-dependent update changes. Selective execution further affects the direction-reversal risk of retained updates. To address this, we propose Set-Valued Group Relative Policy Optimization (SetGRPO). It comprises three modules: (a) Joint Reward Set Calibration constructs a joint uncertainty set for the training coefficients; (b) Geometry-Guided Safe Recovery maps candidate coefficients into the current policy's local update geometry and determines the largest safe recovery ratio for each response group; and (c) Selective Risk-Gated Optimization selects a global threshold through independent risk calibration to control the conditional direction-reversal risk of accepted updates while preserving the original GRPO objective. Under exchangeability, SetGRPO provides finite-sample marginal coverage for the joint coefficient set and simultaneous risk control across candidate thresholds. On ten open-ended benchmarks spanning three domains, SetGRPO achieves the highest macro average among all compared training methods on both Qwen3.5 and Llama3.2 model families.

items.title_en: A fully articulated humanoid dexterous hand with human-level joint structure enabled by linkage-based actuation
items.title_zh: 一种基于连杆驱动、具备人类水平关节结构的全关节仿人灵巧手
items.abstract_en: Humanoid dexterous hands are a core component of embodied intelligence, enabling robots to translate high-level intent into rich and adaptive physical interaction. However, existing designs remain constrained by a persistent trade-off among anthropomorphic kinematic complexity, mechanical robustness, load capacity and control simplicity, limiting dexterous manipulation in unstructured environments. Here we present Torch-Hand, a fully articulated humanoid dexterous hand that replicates the joint structure and motion hierarchy of the human hand with 21 degrees of freedom (DOF), comprising a highly articulated five-DOF thumb and four DOF in each of the remaining fingers. The differentiated thumb integrates multi-axis CMC motion to provide broad opposition and flexible contact orientation relative to the four fingers. Unlike tendon-driven or hybrid actuation approaches, Torch-Hand adopts an entirely linkage-based transmission architecture. By integrating screw-linkage actuation, the hand achieves high grasping force and substantial payload capacity while maintaining a compact anthropomorphic form. Its actuation architecture is optimized for control tractability, with all actuators integrated within the palm and arranged in a serial-robot-like configuration that establishes a direct correspondence between motor motion and joint kinematics. This architecture mechanically decouples functional DOF to reduce unintended inter-joint motion propagation, while allowing independently addressable DOF to be actively coordinated into coupled multi-joint motion patterns during complex manipulation. Comprehensive experiments assess reachable workspace, coordinated fingertip trajectories, thumb opposition, 33-grasp taxonomy coverage, grasping force, payload capacity and task-level manipulation. These results establish Torch-Hand as a robust hardware foundation for dexterous embodied manipulation.

rm.usage: 全关节灵巧手的机械设计对工程机器人末端执行器有一定参考价值，但RM工程装配多用简单夹爪且受规则/负载限制，算法层面几乎用不上。

items.title_en: Frequency-Uniform Log-Regret Reinforcement Learning for Diffusions
items.title_zh: 面向扩散模型的频率均匀对数遗憾强化学习
items.abstract_en: High-frequency control problems are often studied through time discretization, but refining the timestep $δ$ increases the discrete horizon $H=T/δ$ and can make standard finite-horizon regret guarantees deteriorate even when the physical horizon $T$ is fixed. We study episodic value-based reinforcement learning for Euler discretizations of controlled diffusions. The performance is measured as the cumulative regret over $K$ episodes relative to the optimal policy of the corresponding Euler model. Under stability and regularity conditions on value function gradients, Bellman residual derivatives, and fitted critics, we prove an $\mathcal{O}(\log K)$ regret bound with constants uniform in $δ$. For dynamics with drift linear in unknown parameters and unknown constant diffusion covariance, we verify localized versions of these conditions for a constrained, model-based controlled-diffusion fitted-$Q$ algorithm (CD-FQ) and obtain high-probability $\mathcal{O}(\log K\log\log K)$ regret for fixed and finite $T$, again with constants uniform in $δ$.

items.title_en: Learning Side-by-Side Navigation for Personal Mobility Vehicles from Human Drivers
items.title_zh: 从人类驾驶行为中学习个人出行车辆的并排导航
items.abstract_en: This paper presents an approach to achieve side-by-side autonomous motion with a pair of personal mobility vehicles (PMVs). Given a global path, two PMVs plan cooperatively so as to hold a social formation that lets the passengers hold a conversation, while keeping the ride safe and smooth. Each vehicle runs its own sampling-based model-predictive planner; the planners exchange nothing but the odometry each vehicle could observe of the other, and the joint decision is expressed as a pair of utility matrices over pairs of candidate trajectories, resolved by a common rule. The behavioural parameters are fitted by inverse reinforcement learning from 409 minutes of driving by ten pairs of people in human-driven PMVs in an indoor environment, and the lanes the pair can use are derived offline from the corridor itself rather than fixed by hand. A safety layer the cost cannot override executes a move only if the vehicle can still brake clear, measured from its whole body, and a vehicle that is stuck reverses along its own path and continues. In closed-loop simulation over 24 runs in the conditions the drivers were recorded in and 24 in four generated obstacle layouts, no vehicle entered a wall or a cone. The pair holds conversational formation for 60.5 and 68.9 percent of the time among obstacles (anticlockwise and clockwise) and 81.2 and 91.5 percent in a clear aisle, against the drivers' 34.0 and 36.0 percent, and 52.9 and 56.0 percent, and it matches their speed. It keeps one lateral formation where the drivers alternated between a close diagonal and a wide abreast one, and it varies far less. Experimental results are based on a differential drive kinematic simulator running on ROS 2.

items.title_en: On Shaky Ground: Characterising Non-Rigid Base Effects in Mobile Manipulation
items.title_zh: 立足不稳：刻画移动操作中的非刚性基座效应
items.abstract_en: Mobile robot manipulators extend contact-task capability beyond the workspace of fixed robot installations, but their bases must also sustain the forces generated by the task. On lightweight platforms, base motion and support compliance can change the force and motion realised at the workpiece. How these non-rigid base effects manifest during sustained contact remains insufficiently characterised. This paper investigates non-rigid base effects in mobile robot manipulators through a sanding case study combining exploratory simulation with experiments on two lightweight, unactuated wheeled testbeds. Joint measurements of contact force, tool motion, and base vibration show that sustained contact coexisted with substantial task error: under low base-ground resistance, only 54-70% of a 100 N command was realised, with tool-centre-point errors reaching 100 mm. Increasing base-ground resistance during contact improved force realisation and arrested further tool displacement, while base vibration did not vary consistently with force-tracking error in the tested conditions. These observations illustrate how non-rigid base behaviour can affect contact-task execution and highlight the value of examining force, motion, and vibration together when characterising lightweight mobile manipulation.
items.comment: 10 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables. Accepted at the Australasian Conference on Robotics and Automation (ACRA 2026)

items.title_en: TOPS: Reshaping Flow Source and Transport for Multi-Task Robot Manipulation
items.title_zh: TOPS：重塑流源与输运以支持多任务机器人操作
items.abstract_en: Flow-based policies for language-conditioned multi-task manipulation commonly share a single $\textit{Gaussian}$ source prior and a common linear transport path across tasks. However, reliably executing multiple tasks with distinct motion requirements remains challenging for a shared policy. We introduce $\textbf{TOPS}$ ($\textbf{T}$ask-$\textbf{O}$riented $\textbf{P}$riors and $\textbf{S}$chedules), which adapts the flow source prior and interpolation schedule to each task without modifying the network architecture. TOPS first constructs multimodal task sources from reverse-mapped expert action sequences, allowing language instructions to select where generation begins. Guided by source-target covariance mismatch, it then slows the transition toward expert actions early in denoising and accelerates it later along directions requiring expansion. Under a $\textit{Gaussian}$ endpoint model, our analysis shows that this schedule adjustment can lower an upper bound on velocity-prediction risk. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and CALVIN demonstrate improved performance across in-distribution, perturbation and cross-environment settings, alongside better data efficiency. Using one integration step, TOPS raises LIBERO-10 success from $53.44\%$ to $69.67\%$ compared with ten-step Standard Flow Matching (FM), while reducing inference time to approximately one-sixth of the baseline. TOPS also yields consistent gains when transferred to the large-scale flow-based $π_{0.5}$ policy across all four evaluated settings. Real-world experiments further demonstrate improved task success, including an increase from $20\%$ with standard FM to $80\%$ with TOPS on the upper-drawer opening task.

rm.usage: 面向多任务操作的自适应流源先验与插值调度，可思路参考到工程机器人多类装配动作（抓取、对位、插装）的统一策略学习，但与赛场上少样本、强实时需求差距较大。

items.title_en: Quantifying and Prioritizing Stealthy Source-Manipulation Threats Against Multi-Source Anomaly Detectors
items.title_zh: 量化并优先排序针对多源异常检测器的隐蔽源操纵威胁
items.abstract_en: Security pipelines often fuse several data sources and protect a downstream model with a cross-source anomaly detector. Such detectors are usually judged by their clean false-positive rate and by how well they catch random corruption. Neither metric captures an adversary who controls some sources and targets a specific downstream decision. We propose a threat-quantification score, the \emph{task-conditioned visibility margin}, defined as the least detector evidence a manipulation must reveal per unit of harm to the downstream task. The margin has a closed form, takes about $85\,μ$s per certificate, yields a minimum-evidence attack, and identifies task-relevant directions the detector cannot see. On a 17-channel industrial telemetry benchmark, a detector that flags 82.8\% of random single-channel corruptions is first-order blind on 64.7\% of task/subset pairs in an audit of one- to four-channel subsets. Task-conditioned manipulations cause more than twice as many falsely reassuring errors as generic stealthy ones, and more of them evade the alarm on four of five splits, mainly at small budgets. Used to prioritize audits on held-out subsets, the margin finds a median of four verified failures in ten checks, compared with none for random order and two for alarm-based ranking, and performs comparably to the task-gradient baseline. It also ranks vulnerable configurations of the learned GDN and TranAD detectors and of a five-source crop-yield panel.

items.title_en: RoboSTD: Zero-Shot Single-to-Dual Transfer via Sagittal Mirroring for Bimanual Learning
items.title_zh: RoboSTD：通过矢状镜面实现零样本单臂到双臂迁移的双臂学习
items.abstract_en: Bimanual robot manipulation plays an important role in real-world robotic applications, but the high cost of collecting bimanual demonstrations limits the scalable development of bimanual policy learning. Meanwhile, existing single-arm manipulation data are difficult to directly transfer to bimanual systems due to the Single-to-Dual gap in action spaces, coordination requirements, and arm-side spatial preference. To address this issue, we propose RoboSTD, a zero-shot Single-to-Dual data construction method for bimanual robot learning. RoboSTD first applies sagittal-plane mirroring to observations, proprioception, and actions to construct executable contralateral pseudo-demonstrations. It then uses an LLM to generate structured spatio-temporal coordination constraints that guide the reconstruction of pseudo-bimanual supervision across workspace regions and task stages. We evaluate RoboSTD on the AgileX ALOHA platform in both RoboTwin simulation and real-world settings. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of RoboSTD for bimanual policy learning. Without requiring additional bimanual demonstrations, RoboSTD increases the average number of collected cups to 2.11x that of the single-arm baseline in the cup collection task. Project page: https://huahungy.github.io/RoboSTD/

items.title_en: From Biological Curves to Soft Modular Robots: Learning-Based Inverse Design with Uncertainty-Guided Refinement
items.title_zh: 从生物曲线到软体模块化机器人：基于学习与不确定性引导细化的逆向设计
items.abstract_en: Animals exhibit diverse shape-changing behaviors, from the undulatory swimming of eels to the arching movements of inchworms. Reproducing these biological shapes with modular soft robots offers a promising approach to developing versatile bioinspired robotic systems. However, translating a desired shape into a feasible robotic configuration remains challenging. Existing cable-driven modular soft robots rely on computationally expensive physics-based modeling and combinatorial search for inverse design, making it difficult to efficiently reproduce diverse target shapes. To address this challenge, we present a learning-based real-to-sim-to-real framework that translates biological curves into robotic configurations through surrogate-assisted inverse design and uncertainty-guided refinement. The proposed method combines learned inverse prediction with targeted candidate exploration, using a fast forward surrogate to evaluate and select suitable designs. The learned forward surrogate reduces deformation prediction time from $1.53 \times 10^5$ ms to 0.0008 ms, achieving approximately a $1.9 \times 10^8$-fold speedup. At the same time, the proposed inverse design method reduces design time from $1.99 \times 10^6$ ms to 4.18 ms. On 5,000 test samples generated from previously unseen threading patterns, the method achieves a 93% shape reconstruction success rate under surrogate-based evaluation. Physical demonstrations with four bioinspired robots further illustrate the translation of biological curves into realizable robotic shapes.

items.title_en: SWIM: Learning What Matters from Behaviors for JEPA World Models
items.title_zh: SWIM：为 JEPA 世界模型从行为中学习关键信息
items.abstract_en: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) enable world models to plan from images by predicting future embeddings. However, their visual prediction objectives do not explicitly incorporate task-relevant state information, so the physical state that determines task progress may not be reliably captured in the latent space. Supervising world models with simulator state can make planning more informative, but it requires deciding which state features matter. Features are typically selected by hand or weighted uniformly, and a uniform weighting gives every standardized state feature equal influence, so redundant coordinates can overcount the same variation, while irrelevant ones can obscure task-relevant differences. To address this limitation, we propose SWIM (State Weighting with Inverse-Dynamics Model), which learns state weights from offline trajectories by predicting recorded actions from current states and observed future displacements. The learned weights quantify each feature's contribution to action prediction and define a weighted state metric for state-supervised training, which we demonstrate by aligning latent and state distances. The inverse-dynamics model is used only during training, so the resulting world model plans from images with no additional planning-time computation. Across five simulated robotic manipulation tasks, SWIM consistently improves planning success over uniform state weighting.

rm.usage: 从行为中挑选任务相关状态特征来监督 JEPA 世界模型潜在空间，可用于仿真中构造更有效的世界模型/表征，用于强化学习训练策略或预测对抗状态；属于支撑性工具。

items.title_en: Deep Bayesian Approaches for Interpretable Nonlinear Structural System Identification
items.title_zh: 可解释非线性结构系统辨识的深度贝叶斯方法
items.abstract_en: System identification, namely the inference of mathematical representations of dynamical systems from measured data, is fundamental to engineering diagnostics, prognostics, and decision-making. Bayesian filtering offers a principled framework for probabilistic state estimation but traditionally relies on prescribed transition and observation models. Recent advances in deep Bayesian filtering address this limitation by embedding learnable representations within probabilistic state-space formulations, enabling data-driven identification of unknown dynamics while retaining physical structure and uncertainty-aware inference. This tutorial provides a systematic introduction to deep Bayesian filtering for nonlinear structural system identification, focusing on the interplay between learned dynamics, physical inductive biases, and posterior inference. The Deep Markov Model serves as a data-driven reference, while the Physics-guided Deep Markov Model (PgDMM) and Neural Extended Kalman Filter (Neural EKF) illustrate complementary approaches based on amortized variational inference and differentiable Kalman filtering, respectively. Their capabilities are examined through dynamic state estimation and joint dynamic state and parameter estimation on a three-dimensional shear-frame benchmark with hysteretic Bouc-Wen connections and sparse acceleration measurements. The results highlight important distinctions between measurement-conditioned reconstruction and open-loop forecasting, demonstrate how physical structure can improve latent-state interpretability without necessarily ensuring predictive fidelity, and reveal differences in the robustness of response and parameter estimation. Practical guidelines for model construction, training, evaluation, and deployment are provided, together with an outlook on remaining challenges in uncertainty calibration, identifiability, and real-world validation.
